oil.summary: Crude suffered one of its sharpest single-day selloffs of the year, with WTI down 8.0% to $92.22/bbl and Brent off 7.5% to $96.05, unwinding a chunk of last month's gains. RBOB led the complex lower at -9.4%. The catalyst appears to be the emergence of a Houthi-U.S. deal referenced by OilPrice.com, which the market is reading as a de-escalation signal despite ongoing physical disruption: satellite data cited by Bloomberg shows supertankers carrying capacity for 14 million barrels diverted to Saudi Gulf terminals after Houthi strikes targeted Yanbu. Iran's claim of striking a Hormuz tanker and Trump's signing of the Russia-Iran Sanctions Act—authorising up to 100% secondary tariffs on Russian oil buyers including India and China—add headline risk, but today the market voted for de-escalation. Heating oil at $4.69/gal and a separate report flagging fears of local diesel shortages underscore lingering tightness in distillates.
drivers: Houthi-U.S. deal signals perceived de-escalation, triggering sharp risk-off unwind in crude longs
Saudi rerouting of exports to Gulf terminals (14 mn bbl capacity visible via satellite) underscores Yanbu disruption but also supply resilience
Trump signs Russia-Iran Sanctions Act enabling 100% tariffs on Russian oil buyers; China/Russia veto UN Iran sanctions panel extension—competing geopolitical pressures

gas.summary: European and U.S. gas prices both fell sharply on the session—TTF dropped 7.1% to €73.9/MWh despite being up 13% on the month, while Henry Hub slipped 2.4% to $2.84/MMBtu. The Hormuz story remains the dominant structural risk: QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi warned that the Strait of Hormuz crisis could delay Qatar's $83 billion LNG expansion programme because critical equipment cannot be delivered. Pakistan's successful negotiation of safe passage through Hormuz for a second Qatari LNG cargo offers a narrow proof-of-concept that transit deals are possible, but it is a fragile arrangement. The ECB flagged today that wholesale gas price surges are passing through to Eurozone retail and electricity inflation faster than historically, adding policy pressure on European governments. The European Commission meanwhile is expected to maintain its Arctic drilling ban despite Norwegian lobbying, limiting medium-term supply optionality.
drivers: QatarEnergy warns Hormuz crisis threatens $83 bn LNG expansion; Strait transit risk structurally supportive even as prices correct today
ECB cautions on accelerating wholesale-to-retail gas price pass-through in the Eurozone, raising demand-destruction and policy-response risk
Pakistan secures Qatari LNG cargo via negotiated Hormuz safe passage—a fragile workaround that underscores continued supply-route vulnerability

power.summary: EU Carbon (EUA) was broadly flat on the day at $82.44/EUA (-0.1%), consolidating a 5.6% monthly gain, while TTF's 7% decline provides modest near-term relief on gas-fired generation costs. The key power-sector concern today comes from India: nearly 40% of operational coal-fired plants are running on critically low inventory, with coal demand forecast to jump 4.2%—a signal of acute stress in Asian power markets that could redirect global coal and LNG flows. In Europe, the ECB's warning that gas price surges are feeding through to electricity inflation faster than in past cycles puts pressure on regulators; the Czech government's move to reinstate fuel price caps from October 1 and tax Orlen's refining margins is an early example of government intervention spreading. Trump's Russia-Iran sanctions law adds background risk to Russian energy supply chains underpinning European baseload.
drivers: India coal-fired power sector under acute stress: ~40% of plants at critically low inventory, demand set to rise 4.2%—potential LNG and coal diversion away from Europe
ECB warns of faster-than-historical wholesale gas pass-through to Eurozone electricity inflation, elevating demand-side and regulatory risk
EUA flat on day despite TTF decline; Czech fuel price caps and windfall margin tax signal widening European government intervention trend
